page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.6xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine type within the compute-optimized family, designed for specialized parallel processing tasks. Provisioned on the KVM hypervisor, it features an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 24 dedicated vCPUs derived from 12 physical cores using two threads per core. System memory provides 93 GB of RAM, maintaining approximately 3.88 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is supplied by a single NVIDIA T4 GPU based on the Turing architecture, providing 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. The instance operates on an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and includes no local storage, requiring the attachment of external cloud storage volumes.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear separation between general CPU throughput and GPU-accelerated execution. The central processor demonstrates weak to poor single-core performance across Geekbench and stress-ng tests, alongside lower-tier single-threaded compression scores. Multi-core performance scales to median levels, recorded across PassMark CPU evaluations, Clang compilation, and multi-threaded decompression. Memory bandwidth reaches 95.33 GB/s on large uncached read operations. The integrated NVIDIA T4 demonstrates top-tier inference speeds during prompt processing for small 135M and medium 7B models, accompanied by strong text generation throughput on 7B architectures.

The ecs.gn6i-c24g1.6xlarge provides a cost-effective alternative to larger multi-GPU training nodes by pairing an entry-level enterprise inference accelerator with a substantial vCPU count. The lack of bundled local NVMe storage represents a tradeoff, as persistent or scratch disk throughput relies entirely on network-attached storage performance. The server is well positioned for machine learning inference serving, video transcoding, graphic rendering pipelines, and distributed batch computing workloads that leverage Tensor Core acceleration.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.6xlarge is a compute-optimized, GPU-accelerated virtual machine tailored for machine learning inference and parallel processing workloads. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor providing 24 dedicated vCPUs across 12 physical cores at 2.5 GHz, paired with 93 GB of system memory. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA T4 GPU featuring 16 GB of VRAM. It includes an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile and contains no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for persistent data. In benchmark evaluations, the CPU exhibits average multi-core throughput alongside weaker single-core processing scores. The GPU provides top-tier prompt processing performance for small and medium language models, delivering strong generation rates on 7B parameter architectures. This configuration delivers an efficient resource ratio for small-to-midsize model inference, video transcoding, and batch computing pipelines that do not demand multi-GPU configurations.
